title: Paya Soup

seo.title: How to Make Paya Soup — Easy Pakistani Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Paya Soup. This easy Pakistani recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.

seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Paya Soup — a beloved Pakistani classic

description: Paya Soup is a rich, gelatinous Pakistani delicacy, known for its comforting warmth and deep flavors. Made from slow-cooked trotters, it is a hearty and nutritious meal often enjoyed during cold weather or as a special occasion dish. The broth is infused with aromatic spices, creating a truly unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Clean and Prepare Paya
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the goat or lamb trotters, ensuring all hair is removed. You can blanch them briefly in boiling water for easier cleaning if needed. Cut them into manageable pieces.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat oil in a large pressure cooker over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and fry until golden brown. Then add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for another 2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Paya and Spices
instructions.text: Add the cleaned paya pieces to the pressure cooker. Stir well and add red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the paya is lightly seared and coated with spices.

instructions.title: Pressure Cook
instructions.text: Pour in 6-8 cups of water, ensuring the paya is fully submerged. Close the lid of the pressure cooker and cook on high heat until the first whistle, then reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 25 minutes to tenderize the paya quickly.

instructions.title: Final Seasoning
instructions.text: Once the pressure is released naturally, open the cooker. Check if the paya is tender. If not, cook for a few more minutes without the lid or under pressure again. Stir in the garam masala powder.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Paya Soup into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander, slit green chilies, and serve immediately with lemon wedges, naan, or tandoori roti.

tips: For maximum flavor and tender Paya, traditionally, paya is slow-cooked for several hours on low heat. If you have time, consider cooking for 4-6 hours on a stovetop after the initial pressure cooking for an even richer broth.

To achieve a thicker, gelatinous consistency, ensure the paya pieces are well-cleaned and contain plenty of bone marrow. A small amount of wheat flour or gram flour paste can be added at the end, but it is not traditional.
Paya Soup tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, reheating gently before serving.
